requirements.quote:
Initial (Section 17.2.2), 0-RTT (Section 17.2.3), and Handshake
   (Section 17.2.4) packets contain a Length field that determines the
   end of the packet.  The length includes both the Packet Number and
   Payload fields, both of which are confidentiality protected and
   initially of unknown length.  The length of the Payload field is
   learned once header protection is removed.
requirements.condition: For an Initial, 0-RTT, or Handshake packet.
requirements.required_behavior: The packet contains a Length field that determines the end of the packet and whose value includes both the Packet Number and Payload fields.
requirements.why_checkable: Packet encoding and Length-field boundaries can be inspected and compared with the encoded Packet Number and Payload extents.

requirements.quote:
Using the Length field, a sender can coalesce multiple QUIC packets
   into one UDP datagram.  This can reduce the number of UDP datagrams
   needed to complete the cryptographic handshake and start sending
   data.  This can also be used to construct Path Maximum Transmission
   Unit (PMTU) probes; see Section 14.4.1.  Receivers MUST be able to
   process coalesced packets.
requirements.condition: When a UDP datagram contains coalesced QUIC packets.
requirements.required_behavior: A receiver must be able to process the coalesced packets.
requirements.why_checkable: A receiver can be given a datagram containing multiple valid QUIC packets and observed for successful processing.

requirements.quote:
more likely that the receiver will be able to process all the packets
   in a single pass.  A packet with a short header does not include a
   length, so it can only be the last packet included in a UDP datagram.
requirements.condition: When a packet with a short header is included in a UDP datagram.
requirements.required_behavior: The short-header packet must be the last packet in the datagram.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: A sender must not place another packet after a short-header packet in the same UDP datagram.
requirements.why_checkable: The ordering of packet encodings within a UDP datagram can be inspected directly.

requirements.quote:
An endpoint SHOULD include multiple frames in a single packet if they
   are to be sent at the same encryption level, instead of coalescing
   multiple packets at the same encryption level.
requirements.condition: When an endpoint has multiple frames to send at the same encryption level.
requirements.required_behavior: The endpoint should include the frames in one packet.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: The endpoint should avoid coalescing multiple packets at that same encryption level for those frames.
requirements.why_checkable: Generated packets can be inspected to determine whether same-level frames were combined or placed in coalesced same-level packets.

requirements.quote:
Receivers MAY route based on the information in the first packet
   contained in a UDP datagram.  Senders MUST NOT coalesce QUIC packets
requirements.condition: When routing a UDP datagram containing QUIC packets.
requirements.required_behavior: A receiver is permitted to route the datagram using information from its first packet.
requirements.why_checkable: Receiver routing logic can be inspected or exercised to verify that first-packet information is an accepted routing input.

requirements.quote:
contained in a UDP datagram.  Senders MUST NOT coalesce QUIC packets
   with different connection IDs into a single UDP datagram.  Receivers
requirements.condition: When a sender coalesces QUIC packets into one UDP datagram.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: The sender must not coalesce packets with different connection IDs into the same UDP datagram.
requirements.why_checkable: Connection IDs of all packets emitted in a coalesced datagram can be compared.

requirements.quote:
with different connection IDs into a single UDP datagram.  Receivers
   SHOULD ignore any subsequent packets with a different Destination
   Connection ID than the first packet in the datagram.
requirements.condition: When a packet after the first packet in a UDP datagram has a Destination Connection ID different from that of the first packet.
requirements.required_behavior: The receiver should ignore that subsequent packet.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: The receiver should not process that subsequent packet as part of the datagram.
requirements.why_checkable: A crafted datagram with differing subsequent Destination Connection IDs can verify whether those packets are ignored.

requirements.quote:
Every QUIC packet that is coalesced into a single UDP datagram is
   separate and complete.  The receiver of coalesced QUIC packets MUST
   individually process each QUIC packet and separately acknowledge
   them, as if they were received as the payload of different UDP
   datagrams.
requirements.condition: When multiple QUIC packets are coalesced into one UDP datagram.
requirements.required_behavior: Each coalesced QUIC packet must be encoded as a separate and complete packet.
requirements.why_checkable: Each packet boundary in the datagram can be parsed independently and checked for a complete packet encoding.

requirements.quote:
Every QUIC packet that is coalesced into a single UDP datagram is
   separate and complete.  The receiver of coalesced QUIC packets MUST
   individually process each QUIC packet and separately acknowledge
   them, as if they were received as the payload of different UDP
   datagrams.
requirements.condition: When a receiver receives coalesced QUIC packets in one UDP datagram.
requirements.required_behavior: The receiver must process each QUIC packet individually, as if each packet arrived in a different UDP datagram.
requirements.why_checkable: Per-packet processing events can be observed for a datagram containing multiple independently valid packets.

requirements.quote:
Every QUIC packet that is coalesced into a single UDP datagram is
   separate and complete.  The receiver of coalesced QUIC packets MUST
   individually process each QUIC packet and separately acknowledge
   them, as if they were received as the payload of different UDP
   datagrams.
requirements.condition: When received coalesced QUIC packets require acknowledgment.
requirements.required_behavior: The receiver must acknowledge the packets separately, as if each packet arrived in a different UDP datagram.
requirements.why_checkable: Acknowledgment state or emitted ACK frames can be checked for independent acknowledgment of the coalesced packets.

requirements.quote:
datagrams.  For example, if decryption fails (because the keys are
   not available or for any other reason), the receiver MAY either
   discard or buffer the packet for later processing and MUST attempt to

requirements.condition: When decryption of one packet in a coalesced UDP datagram fails.
requirements.required_behavior: The receiver is permitted either to discard the failed packet or to buffer it for later processing.
requirements.error_behavior: The failed packet may be discarded or buffered for later processing.
requirements.why_checkable: A test can force decryption failure and observe whether the receiver selects one of the two permitted dispositions.

requirements.quote:
datagrams.  For example, if decryption fails (because the keys are
   not available or for any other reason), the receiver MAY either
   discard or buffer the packet for later processing and MUST attempt to
   process the remaining packets.
requirements.condition: When decryption of one packet in a coalesced UDP datagram fails.
requirements.required_behavior: The receiver must attempt to process all remaining packets in the datagram.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: The receiver must not stop processing the datagram solely because one packet could not be decrypted.
requirements.error_behavior: Continue attempting to process the remaining packets despite the decryption failure.
requirements.why_checkable: A datagram can place a decryptable packet after an undecryptable packet and test whether processing of the later packet is attempted.

requirements.quote:
Retry packets (Section 17.2.5), Version Negotiation packets
   (Section 17.2.1), and packets with a short header (Section 17.3) do
   not contain a Length field and so cannot be followed by other packets
   in the same UDP datagram.
requirements.condition: When a Retry, Version Negotiation, or short-header packet is present in a UDP datagram.
requirements.required_behavior: That packet must be the final packet in the UDP datagram.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: No other packet may follow it in the same UDP datagram.
requirements.why_checkable: Packet types and their positions within the datagram can be parsed and checked.

requirements.quote:
in the same UDP datagram.  Note also that there is no situation where
   a Retry or Version Negotiation packet is coalesced with another
   packet.
requirements.condition: When constructing or accepting a UDP datagram containing a Retry or Version Negotiation packet.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: A Retry or Version Negotiation packet must not be coalesced with any other packet.
requirements.why_checkable: A datagram containing either packet type can be inspected to ensure it contains no additional QUIC packet.
